cards.text: Elisha, the LORD's prophet in Israel, comes to Damascus. Over there, Ben-hadad, king of Aram, is sick. And word gets to the king: 'The man of God has come here.'
So the king calls Hazael, one of his men, and tells him to take a gift, go meet the man of God, and ask the LORD something through him. The king has ONE question on his mind.

cards.question: Ben-hadad is sick, and the man of God is in town. What does the king want Hazael to ask the LORD through Elisha?

answers.text: Whether he will recover from this illness
Who will reign over Aram after him

cards.question: Hazael goes to meet Elisha with a gift of forty camel loads of every good thing from Damascus.

cards.text: Back on the Millers' counter, ONE plate of cookies for a new neighbor was us going ALL out, and this man rolls up with FORTY CAMELS! Hazael stands before Elisha and asks the king's question, word for word.

cards.question: Hazael asks Elisha whether the king will recover. What does Elisha tell Hazael to go say to the king?
Then Elisha adds one more thing for Hazael: the LORD has shown him that in fact Ben-hadad will ___.

cards.text: Then Elisha fixes his gaze on Hazael and keeps it there until Hazael gets uncomfortable. You know when the boss says 'Got a minute?' and then just LOOKS at you... for WAY more than a minute?

cards.question: After that long, steady stare at Hazael, Elisha the man of God begins to ___.

cards.text: Hazael asks him, 'Why is my lord weeping?' Friend, a prophet staring at me and crying? I'd be asking too. LOUDLY.

cards.question: Why is Elisha weeping as he looks at Hazael?

answers.text: He knows the evil Hazael will do to Israel
He misses his home and family in Israel
He cannot accept such a large gift

cards.text: Elisha spells it out. Hazael will set fire to Israel's fortresses and kill their young men with the sword, and he won't spare the little ones or the pregnant women.

cards.question: Hazael hears this and asks how he, calling himself a mere dog, could do such a monstrous thing.
Elisha answers Hazael with something else the LORD has shown him. What is it?

answers.text: Hazael will be king over Aram
Hazael will fall in battle soon

cards.text: So Hazael leaves Elisha and goes back to his master. And the king's first question is the one you'd expect: what did Elisha say?

cards.question: Hazael answers the sick king that Elisha told him he would surely ___.

cards.text: That's all he tells him. Then the next day, Hazael takes a thick cloth, dips it in water, and spreads it over the king's face.

cards.question: Ben-hadad king of Aram dies. Who reigns in his place?

cards.text: The king who asked if he'd recover dies, just as the LORD showed Elisha. And the man who called himself a mere dog now reigns over Aram, just as the LORD showed Elisha too.

findings.problem: The king's question is whether he will recover. Only the right answer ('You will surely recover') answers it. 'Make peace with Israel' and 'Send for me tomorrow' don't address recovery at all, so the right answer stands out by elimination. The wrong answers should be other believable replies to the recovery question.

rule.text: All the answers are the same kind of thing, about the same length and the same tone. None are silly.

findings.problem: The wrong answer 'rest' is close to the right answer 'die'. Scripture often uses rest for death, as in 'you will rest' in Dan 12:13. A baker could argue that 'Ben-hadad will rest' means he will die.

rule.text: No near-matches. A wrong answer never means the same as the right answer, or close to it. If a baker could argue it's right, replace it.

findings.problem: This story card has four sentences: "Hazael asks him, 'Why is my lord weeping?'" / "Friend, a prophet staring at me and crying?" / "I'd be asking too." / "LOUDLY." Story cards after the opening card are limited to 1 to 2 sentences.

rule.text: Every other story card is 1 to 2 sentences.

findings.problem: The last card is a recap of 2 Kings 8:10-15. It restates that the king dies and that Hazael reigns, which cards 7, 14, 17 and 18 already covered. It doesn't move the passage forward. The passage isn't in a story group, so no continuation line is needed either. The card should be cut, or the passage should end on card 18.
